sections.h2: How quickly can a Yorktown house change hands?
sections.html:
Local sellers choose among a broker, a private sale and a cash buyer who accepts the house unchanged. Yorktown sits on the northern edge of Westchester County, about 38 miles from midtown Manhattan. It is a town, so you deal with the receiver of taxes, the assessor and the building inspector in place of a city hall.

The town is made up of five business hamlets, and no train runs inside its borders. Buyers weigh commute time, school district and the age of the mechanical systems, which makes the records you can hand over early the main factor in closing speed.

Most Yorktown households own, and incomes run high. The July 1, 2025 estimate of 35,944 people is 1.7 percent under the 2020 base of 36,562.

About 95 percent of residents did not move in the past year, which points to long ownership. Rail commuters drive to Katonah on the Harlem Line or Peekskill on the Hudson Line.

Yorktown is bordered by Putnam Valley in Putnam County to the north, Somers to the east, New Castle to the south and Cortlandt to the west, and the Croton River crosses its south end.

  • Yorktown Heights, the mailing address of Town Hall.
  • Jefferson Valley, site of the Jefferson Valley Mall.
  • Shrub Oak, Mohegan Lake and Crompond, part of which lies in Cortlandt.

Franklin D. Roosevelt State Park and the North County Trailway, built on the old New York and Putnam rail bed, are the best known open spaces and worth naming in a listing.

School levy depends on which of four districts your parcel is in. Yorktown Central covers a large part of town, and the rest goes to Lakeland Central, Croton-Harmon Union Free or Ossining Union Free.

The town receiver collects school tax on behalf of all four but has no say over their budgets. Confirm the district before you list, and tell buyers which one applies.

sections.h2: Older houses and the systems buyers check
sections.html: Winters here are hard on a house, so inspectors look first at the roof, the driveway and the heating plant. A recent furnace and roof, backed by receipts, make a better first impression than the same house without paperwork.

Fire, parks, sewer and water district charges are billed by the town's Receiver of Taxes, who also collects county and school tax. Tax is still owed when a bill goes missing.

  • School tax covers July 1 to June 30. A single bill goes out September 1 with two stubs, the first payable September 30 and the second January 31. When a due date lands on a weekend it moves to the next business day, so the 2027 second half is due February 1.
  • A late first school half starts at 2 percent in October and rises in steps to 12 percent, which then holds until the property is sold.
  • Town and county tax goes out April 1 and is due April 30. A late payment starts at 2 percent in May, reaches 5 percent for June and July, and tops out at 12 percent after December.

Nothing extra is charged on the second school half through January, but 10 percent applies in February and March. No reminder goes out in January, and the town has no power to waive penalties. A mailed check needs a genuine post office postmark on or before the due date. Because machine postmarks show the day mail is first processed at a regional facility, put the envelope in the mail days ahead. Pay in person at the Tax Office, 363 Underhill Avenue, any weekday from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., or use the green drop box behind Town Hall.

The filing window opens June 1 and closes on Grievance Day, the third Tuesday of June. For the 2027 roll that is 8 p.m. on June 15, 2027, and the Board of Assessment Review meets at Town Hall from 4 to 8 p.m. that evening. There is no filing fee and no need for an attorney.

Back up the complaint with sales of comparable houses in your neighborhood and school district within a year of the July 1, 2026 valuation date, or with an appraisal. Emailed filings are refused. You can deliver by hand, mail, FedEx, UPS or the drop box at the rear entrance of Town Hall, and the board mails its determination on September 15, 2027.

Each property transfer is reviewed by the assessor, who records the buyer, seller and price. Senior citizens, STAR, military service and agricultural exemptions are the common ones. The assessor can be reached at 914-962-5722, extension 2.

The Building Inspector enforces the town's zoning ordinance and the State building codes, issues permits and certificates of occupancy, and may order unsafe buildings condemned. Applications filed on or after December 31, 2025 are measured against the 2025 editions of the State codes. Hours are weekdays 7:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. at Town Hall.

The town warns that it never tells anyone to wire a development fee. Fees are paid by check to the Town of Yorktown under the master fee schedule.

Buyers here worry about the age of the house, so show them proof. Get permits and certificates of occupancy from the Building Department, find the receipts for the roof and furnace, and print the newest school and town bills. The Tax Office will tell you what is paid, and the assessor will tell you which exemptions sit on the parcel.

With cash there is no lender appraisal, and the house is taken as is, so you skip repairs. Payoff, transfer forms and county recording are unchanged. Your attorney can prepare them in parallel with your gathering of documents.

sections.h2: Sorting out a sale with a closing attorney
sections.html:
Two clocks govern the closing. One is the tax calendar, which settles who owes which bill, and the other is the county clerk's document list, which sets how soon the deed can be filed. If the school tax second half falls due soon after your closing date, ask the attorney to work out the split and to show the payoff in writing.

If the title has more than one name on it, make sure every owner is available to sign. An estate or a divorce can add weeks, and a cash buyer cannot shorten that part. Put the question to your attorney on day one so there are no surprises later.

Every Yorktown deed is filed through the Land Records Division of the Westchester County Clerk. Bring four documents from the clerk's PREP portal: recording cover page, TP-584, RP-5217 and payment cover page.

New York's transfer tax is $2 for every $500 of the price, rounded up to the next $500, due when the deed is presented. The seller usually pays, though the contract can say otherwise. Once a home reaches $1 million, the buyer owes an extra 1 percent.

faqs.q: When is the second half of Yorktown school tax due?
faqs.a: January 31. A weekend date moves to the next business day, so the 2027 second half is due Monday, February 1.

faqs.q: What penalty applies to Yorktown town and county tax paid in June?
faqs.a: The penalty is 5 percent. The bill is due April 30, adds 2 percent in May and 5 percent in June and July, and the town says it cannot waive any of it.

faqs.q: How do I contest my Yorktown assessment?
faqs.a: File with the Assessment Office between June 1 and Grievance Day, which is June 15, 2027, attaching comparable sales or an appraisal. The office takes no email filings.

faqs.q: Which Yorktown office issues certificates of occupancy?
faqs.a: The Building Department at Town Hall, 363 Underhill Avenue, headed by the Building Inspector, who also issues permits and enforces zoning and State codes.

faqs.q: Who pays state transfer tax on a Yorktown sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays unless the contract shifts it to the buyer. The tax is $2 for each $500 of price, rounded up to the next $500.
